1 # Python-Markdown: Architecture 2 3 This document describes how the `markdown` package is put together: its main components, three key design decisions (ADRs), and the rules a developer should keep to when changing the code. 4 5 ## 1. Overview 6 7 Python-Markdown turns Markdown text into (X)HTML through a fixed **five-stage pipeline** driven by the `Markdown` class. Each stage is a **priority-ordered registry of processors**. All behaviour, built-in or added, comes from the processors in those registries. **Extensions** change the converter by registering, replacing or removing processors; they never change the pipeline itself. The package has no runtime third-party dependencies (`pyproject.toml` declares none). 8 9 ### Components 10 11 | # | Component | Files | Responsibility | 12 |---|-----------|-------|----------------| 13 | 1 | **Core** | `core.py`, `__init__.py`, `__main__.py` | Public API (`markdown()`, `markdownFromFile()`, `Markdown`, `convert()`, `convertFile()`, the `markdown_py` CLI). `build_parser()` creates the five registries; `registerExtensions()`/`build_extension()` load extensions. Holds shared per-instance state: `htmlStash`, `references`, `ESCAPED_CHARS`, `block_level_elements`, `output_format`/`serializer`. `reset()` clears the per-document state. | 14 | 2 | **Preprocessors** | `preprocessors.py`, `htmlparser.py` | Work on the source as a list of lines before parsing. Defaults: `normalize_whitespace` (30) and `html_block` (20). The latter uses `HTMLExtractor` (`htmlparser.py`) to move raw HTML blocks into the `htmlStash`. | 15 | 3 | **Block parser** | `blockparser.py`, `blockprocessors.py` | `BlockParser.parseDocument()` creates the root element (`md.doc_tag`, a `div`), splits the text into blocks on blank lines, and for each block asks every `BlockProcessor` in priority order whether it applies (`test()`), then calls `run()`. Processors build `ElementTree` elements and may recurse through `parser.parseChunk()`/`parseBlocks()`. A `State` stack (`parser.state`) tracks nesting such as lists. Defaults: `empty` 100, `indent` 90, `code` 80, `hashheader` 70, `setextheader` 60, `hr` 50, `olist` 40, `ulist` 30, `quote` 20, `reference` 15, `paragraph` 10. | 16 | 4 | **Tree processors** | `treeprocessors.py` | Work on the whole `ElementTree` after block parsing. Defaults: `inline` 20 (runs the inline patterns), `prettify` 10 (adds whitespace and newlines), `unescape` 0 (turns backslash-escape placeholders back into characters). | 17 | 5 | **Inline patterns** | `inlinepatterns.py` | Regex-based `InlineProcessor` subclasses whose `handleMatch(m, data)` returns `(element_or_text, start, end)`. The `inline` tree processor applies them to each element's text in priority order. Defaults: `backtick` 190, `escape` 180, `reference` 170, `link` 160, `image_link` 150, `image_reference` 140, `short_reference` 130, `short_image_ref` 125, `autolink` 120, `automail` 110, `linebreak` 100, `html` 90, `entity` 80, `em_strong` 60 (a `DelimiterProcessor` for `*` and `_`). | 18 | 6 | **Serializers and postprocessors** | `serializers.py`, `postprocessors.py` | The serializer (`to_xhtml_string` by default, or `to_html_string`) turns the tree into a string and escapes text and attributes. Postprocessors then work on that string: `raw_html` 30 (replaces stash placeholders with the stored HTML) and `amp_substitute` 20. | 19 | 7 | **Utilities** | `util.py` | Shared building blocks: `Registry`, the `Processor` base class, `AtomicString`, `HtmlStash`, placeholder templates (`STX`/`ETX`-delimited), `BLOCK_LEVEL_ELEMENTS`, and the entry-point lookup `get_installed_extensions()`. | 20 | 8 | **Extensions** | `extensions/__init__.py`, `extensions/*.py` | The `Extension` base class (config handling plus `extendMarkdown(md)`) and 18 built-in extensions (e.g. `tables`, `footnotes`, `def_list`, `fenced_code`, `codehilite`, `admonition`, `smarty`, `meta`). `extra` is a bundle that loads several others. | 21 22 ### How the components call each other 23 24 ```mermaid 25 flowchart LR 26 U["markdown() / Markdown.convert()"] --> C["Core: Markdown"] 27 C -- "__init__: build_parser()" --> R[("Registries (util.Registry)")] 28 C -- "registerExtensions()" --> E["Extensions: extendMarkdown(md)"] 29 E -- "register / deregister" --> R 30 31 subgraph Pipeline["convert(): the five stages"] 32 direction LR 33 P["1. Preprocessors
lines → lines"] --> B["2. BlockParser + BlockProcessors
lines → ElementTree"] 34 B --> T["3. Treeprocessors
tree → tree"] 35 T --> S["4. Serializer
tree → string"] 36 S --> PP["5. Postprocessors
string → string"] 37 T -. "'inline' runs" .-> I["Inline patterns"] 38 end 39 C --> P 40 PP --> O["HTML output"] 41 42 H[("md.htmlStash
md.references")] 43 P -. "store raw HTML" .-> H 44 B -. "store link refs" .-> H 45 I -. "read refs / store HTML" .-> H 46 PP -. "restore raw HTML" .-> H 47 ``` 48 49 Processors reach shared state through the `Markdown` instance. Block processors use `self.parser.md`. Other processors receive it as the optional `md` constructor argument (`self.md`). Built-ins that need no shared state are created without it (e.g. `backtick`, `linebreak`, `amp_substitute`), so a processor that uses `self.md` must be constructed with `md`. Dependencies point one way: `util.py` imports no other module of the package at runtime (only a type-checking import of `Markdown`); the core stage modules depend on `util.py`; extensions depend on the core modules; the core never imports a specific extension. 50 51 ## 2. Architecture Decision Records 52 53 ### ADR-1: A priority-sorted `Registry` for every processing stage 54 55 **Status:** Verified. Commit `6ee07d2` (2018), *"Replace homegrown OrderedDict with purpose-built Registry. (#688)"*, which fixes issue #418. The deprecated compatibility shim was removed in commit `a767b2d` (2022, *"Remove previously deprecated objects"*). Implementation: `markdown/util.py`, class `Registry`. 56 57 **Context.** Processors used to live in a home-grown `OrderedDict` where each item was placed relative to another by a location string (`"_begin"`, `"name"`). Placement depended on which other items happened to be present and on the order extensions were loaded, which made combining extensions fragile. 58 59 **Decision.** Every stage (`preprocessors`, `parser.blockprocessors`, `inlinePatterns`, `treeprocessors`, `postprocessors`) is a `util.Registry`. Items are registered with a **name** and a numeric **priority** and are iterated from highest to lowest priority. Items with equal priority keep their registration order. Registering an existing name replaces the old item, which is then sorted by its new priority. `deregister(name)` removes an item. Items can be looked up by name or index. 60 61 **Alternatives considered.** (a) Keep the relative-location `OrderedDict` API. It was kept only as a deprecated shim and later removed. (b) Use plain lists that extensions insert into by index, which has the same load-order fragility. 62 63 **Consequences.** Placement is independent of load order, and any built-in processor can be replaced or removed by name. On the other hand, priorities act as global "magic numbers": to place a new processor correctly, an author must know the priorities of the built-ins it has to run before or after (listed in §1). 64 65 ### ADR-2: Extensions are found by entry point, with a dotted-path fallback 66 67 **Status:** Verified. Commit `cd73243` (2018), *"Refactor Extension loading (#627)"*. Implementation: `Markdown.build_extension()` in `markdown/core.py` and `util.get_installed_extensions()` in `markdown/util.py`; built-in names are declared in `pyproject.toml`. 68 69 **Context.** Short names such as `'tables'` used to be special-cased to modules inside `markdown.extensions`, and there was also an `mdx_` module-prefix convention. Third-party authors who wanted short names told users to copy files into the package. 70 71 **Decision.** A string name passed in `extensions=[...]` is first looked up in the `markdown.extensions` **entry-point group** of the installed distributions. If no entry point matches, the string is treated as a dotted import path `package.module[:ClassName]`. Without a class name, the module's `makeExtension(**kwargs)` is called. Extension *instances* may also be passed directly. All built-ins are declared under `[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']` in `pyproject.toml`. 72 73 **Alternatives considered.** (a) Keep special-casing the `markdown.extensions` package and the `mdx_` prefix (removed in this change). (b) Require full dotted paths for everything, which would break existing short names. 74 75 **Consequences.** Third-party extensions get short names on the same terms as built-ins, and dotted paths still work without packaging. On the other hand, a short name exists only in **installed** package metadata: a new or renamed entry point takes effect only after the distribution is (re)installed, and until then the string is treated as a module path. 76 77 ### ADR-3: `ElementTree` as the document model; raw HTML and protected text kept out of reach 78 79 **Status:** Inferred. The switch is recorded (commit `a218ebb`, 2008, *"ElementTree support added"*, which replaced the earlier home-grown `NanoDom`), `serializers.py` says it was *"taken from ElementTree 1.3 preview"*, and the `HtmlStash` docstring describes the stash. No commit or issue states the *reasons*, so the rationale below is our own reading of the code. 80 81 **Context.** A Markdown document mixes structure (paragraphs, lists, emphasis) with raw HTML that must pass through untouched. A pipeline of string substitutions (the original `Markdown.pl` approach) gives later steps no view of the structure and can easily process the same text twice. 82 83 **Decision.** Block parsing builds an `xml.etree.ElementTree`. Later stages work on elements, and the package's own serializers produce HTML or XHTML. Content that must not be treated as Markdown is kept out of reach in two ways. (1) **Raw HTML** is not put into the tree: it is stored in `md.htmlStash` and replaced by a placeholder (`STX + "wzxhzdk:N" + ETX`), which the `raw_html` postprocessor swaps back after serialization. (2) **Text that must not be processed by further inline patterns** is wrapped in `util.AtomicString`, which the `inline` tree processor skips. Backslash escapes follow the same idea: the `escape` pattern replaces an escaped character with an `STX`/`ETX` placeholder, and the `unescape` tree processor restores it at the end. 84 85 **Alternatives considered.** (a) A string-only pipeline. (b) The earlier custom DOM (`NanoDom`). (c) Parsing raw HTML into the tree, which would need a full HTML parser and would normalise or re-escape the user's HTML. 86 87 **Consequences.** Extensions can inspect and rewrite structure with tree processors, and output escaping happens in one place, the serializer. On the other hand, content travels on two channels, the tree and the stash, and developers must use the right one. Text placed in an element is escaped on output, so markup must be stored in the stash or built as elements. Placeholders also appear as ordinary text inside the tree, so tree processors see placeholders rather than the HTML behind them. 88 89 ## 3. Constraints 90 91 | # | Rule | Where it is visible | 92 |---|------|---------------------| 93 | C1 | **Change the pipeline only through the Registry API.** Add, replace or remove processors with `register(item, name, priority)` / `deregister(name)` on the instance's registries (`md.preprocessors`, `md.parser.blockprocessors`, `md.inlinePatterns`, `md.treeprocessors`, `md.postprocessors`). Do not edit the default `build_*` functions to add optional behaviour, and choose priorities relative to the built-ins. | `markdown/util.py` (`Registry`); `markdown/core.py` (`build_parser`); defaults in the `build_*` functions of each stage module | 94 | C2 | **Extensions follow the extension contract.** Subclass `markdown.extensions.Extension`, declare options as `self.config = {name: [default, description]}` before calling `super().__init__(**kwargs)`, read them with `getConfig`/`getConfigs`, do all wiring in `extendMarkdown(md)`, and provide a module-level `makeExtension(**kwargs)`. Built-ins live in `markdown/extensions/` and are listed as entry points in `pyproject.toml`. | `markdown/extensions/__init__.py`; `pyproject.toml` (`[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']`); any built-in such as `markdown/extensions/admonition.py` | 95 | C3 | **Dependencies point one way.** Core modules (`core.py`, `blockparser.py`, `blockprocessors.py`, `inlinepatterns.py`, `treeprocessors.py`, `preprocessors.py`, `postprocessors.py`, `serializers.py`, `util.py`) must not import any specific extension module. The only extension imports in the core are of the `Extension` base class (in `core.py` and the package `__init__.py`). Extensions may import core modules. | Import blocks of `markdown/core.py` and `markdown/__init__.py`; imports of the other core modules | 96 | C4 | **Use the right channel for protected content.** Raw HTML that must reach the output unchanged goes through `md.htmlStash.store()`. Text that later inline patterns must not touch is an `util.AtomicString`. Never put pre-rendered HTML into element text or attributes: the serializer will escape it. | `markdown/util.py` (`AtomicString`, `HtmlStash`); `markdown/treeprocessors.py` (`InlineProcessor` skips `AtomicString`); `markdown/postprocessors.py` (`RawHtmlPostprocessor`) | 97 | C5 | **Per-document state must be resettable.** One `Markdown` instance may convert many documents. State that belongs to one document lives on the instance (e.g. `htmlStash`, `references`) or on an extension. An extension with such state calls `md.registerExtension(self)` and implements `reset()`, which `Markdown.reset()` calls. | `markdown/core.py` (`registerExtension`, `reset`) | 98

2	# ======================================
3	
4	# Converts [[WikiLinks]] to relative links.
5	
6	# See https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/wikilinks
7	# for documentation.
8	
9	# Original code Copyright [Waylan Limberg](https://github.com/waylan).
10	
11	# All changes Copyright The Python Markdown Project
12	
13	# License: [BSD](https://opensource.org/licenses/bsd-license.php)
14	
15	"""
16	Converts `[[WikiLinks]]` to relative links.
17	
18	See the [documentation](https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/wikilinks)
19	for details.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	from . import Extension
25	from ..inlinepatterns import InlineProcessor
26	import xml.etree.ElementTree as etree
27	import re
28	from typing import Any
29	
30	
31	def build_url(label: str, base: str, end: str) -> str:
32	    """ Build a URL from the label, a base, and an end. """
33	    clean_label = re.sub(r'([ ]+_)|(_[ ]+)|([ ]+)', '_', label)
34	    return '{}{}{}'.format(base, clean_label, end)
35	
36	
37	class WikiLinkExtension(Extension):
38	    """ Add inline processor to Markdown. """
39	
40	    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
41	        self.config = {
42	            'base_url': ['/', 'String to append to beginning or URL.'],
43	            'end_url': ['/', 'String to append to end of URL.'],
44	            'html_class': ['wikilink', 'CSS hook. Leave blank for none.'],
45	            'build_url': [build_url, 'Callable formats URL from label.'],
46	        }
47	        """ Default configuration options. """
48	        super().__init__(**kwargs)
49	
50	    def extendMarkdown(self, md):
51	        """ Register the processor.
52

# WikiLinks Extension for Python-Markdown
# ======================================

# Converts [[WikiLinks]] to relative links.

# See https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/wikilinks
# for documentation.

# Original code Copyright [Waylan Limberg](https://github.com/waylan).

# All changes Copyright The Python Markdown Project

# License: [BSD](https://opensource.org/licenses/bsd-license.php)

"""
Converts `[[WikiLinks]]` to relative links.

See the [documentation](https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/wikilinks)
for details.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from . import Extension
from ..inlinepatterns import InlineProcessor
import xml.etree.ElementTree as etree
import re
from typing import Any


def build_url(label: str, base: str, end: str) -> str:
    """ Build a URL from the label, a base, and an end. """
    clean_label = re.sub(r'([ ]+_)|(_[ ]+)|([ ]+)', '_', label)
    return '{}{}{}'.format(base, clean_label, end)


class WikiLinkExtension(Extension):
    """ Add inline processor to Markdown. """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self.config = {
            'base_url': ['/', 'String to append to beginning or URL.'],
            'end_url': ['/', 'String to append to end of URL.'],
            'html_class': ['wikilink', 'CSS hook. Leave blank for none.'],
            'build_url': [build_url, 'Callable formats URL from label.'],
        }
        """ Default configuration options. """
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def extendMarkdown(self, md):
        """ Register the processor.

        | Class Instance                                                              | Registry                                                         | Name   | Priority |
        | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | :------: |
        | [`WikiLinksInlineProcessor`][markdown.extensions.wikilinks.WikiLinksInlineProcessor] | [`inlinepatterns`][markdown.inlinepatterns.build_inlinepatterns] | `wikilink` | `75` |

        """
        # flake8: noqa: E501 53-55
        self.md = md

        # append to end of inline patterns
        WIKILINK_RE = r'\[\[([\w0-9_ -]+)\]\]'
        wikilinkPattern = WikiLinksInlineProcessor(WIKILINK_RE, self.getConfigs())
        wikilinkPattern.md = md
        md.inlinePatterns.register(wikilinkPattern, 'wikilink', 75)


class WikiLinksInlineProcessor(InlineProcessor):
    """ Build link from `wikilink`. """

    def __init__(self, pattern: str, config: dict[str, Any]):
        super().__init__(pattern)
        self.config = config

    def handleMatch(self, m: re.Match[str], data: str) -> tuple[etree.Element | str, int, int]:
        if m.group(1).strip():
            base_url, end_url, html_class = self._getMeta()
            label = m.group(1).strip()
            url = self.config['build_url'](label, base_url, end_url)
            a = etree.Element('a')
            a.text = label
            a.set('href', url)
            if html_class:
                a.set('class', html_class)
        else:
            a = ''
        return a, m.start(0), m.end(0)

    def _getMeta(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        """ Return meta data or `config` data. """
        base_url = self.config['base_url']
        end_url = self.config['end_url']
        html_class = self.config['html_class']
        if hasattr(self.md, 'Meta'):
            if 'wiki_base_url' in self.md.Meta:
                base_url = self.md.Meta['wiki_base_url'][0]
            if 'wiki_end_url' in self.md.Meta:
                end_url = self.md.Meta['wiki_end_url'][0]
            if 'wiki_html_class' in self.md.Meta:
                html_class = self.md.Meta['wiki_html_class'][0]
        return base_url, end_url, html_class


def makeExtension(**kwargs):  # pragma: no cover
    return WikiLinkExtension(**kwargs)

# Python-Markdown Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to the
[Python Version Specification](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
See the [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) for details.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

* Support automatic links with URL schemes other than HTTP and FTP, such as
  `<ssh://example.org>` (#1244).
* Fix quadratic-time id generation in the `toc` extension when many headers
  share the same text.
* Ignore glossary abbreviations with empty definitions after inline elements,
  consistently with abbreviations before inline elements.
* Strip complete HTML tags with quoted `>` characters from `toc` labels and
  generated heading IDs.
* Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in `attr_list` when a block ends with an
  unclosed attribute list followed by a long run of spaces, e.g. a line
  consisting only of `{` and some text with many trailing spaces (#1656).
* Fix quadratic-time regex backtracking in hash headers when a long run of `#`
  characters is followed by more text on the same line.
* Fix quadratic time when a document contains many unclosed HTML comments (`<!--`
  with no matching `-->`).
* Fix regression in `BacktickInlineProcessor` where text could be lost when opening
  and closing backticks did not match (#1668).
* Escape the language name in the `codehilite` extension's non-Pygments output to
  maintain consistency with Pygments output.
* Preserve attributes without a value in the `attr_list` extension exactly as
  provided, rather than rendering them as `key="key"`, so the same source
  renders consistently under both the `html` and `xhtml` output formats
  (#1501).

# Design: Wikilinks piped link text `[[Page Name|link text]]` ## Approach Change one regex and one method in the `wikilinks` extension. Nothing in the pipeline changes. 1. **Extend the pattern.** In `WikiLinkExtension.extendMarkdown`, `WIKILINK_RE` gets an optional second group after a single `|`: `r'\[\[([\w0-9_ -]+)(?:\|([^\[\]|\n]*))?\]\]'` - Group 1 is the page name. Its character set stays the same, so plain links are unaffected (out of scope to change). - Group 2 is the link text. It is "anything except `[`, `]`, `|` and newline" (ASSUMP-001 / Q-001 option a). - Group 2 cannot contain `|`, so `[[a|b|c]]` fails to match and stays literal text (ASSUMP-003). - Neither class overlaps with `|`, and the optional group is anchored by `]]`, so there is no quadratic backtracking. 2. **Use the link text in `WikiLinksInlineProcessor.handleMatch`.** - The guard and `label` stay based on `m.group(1).strip()`. An empty page name still returns `''` (ASSUMP-002). - The URL is still `self.config['build_url'](label, base_url, end_url)`, with `base_url`, `end_url` and `html_class` from `_getMeta()`. So `href`, `class`, a custom `build_url` and the `wiki_*` meta-data overrides all come from the page name only (ASSUMP-005: same signature). - Only `a.text` changes: `text = (m.group(2) or '').strip()`, then `a.text = text or label`. Empty or whitespace-only text, or a missing pipe, falls back to the page name. 3. **Docs.** Describe the syntax in `docs/extensions/wikilinks.md` and add an entry to `docs/changelog.md` under `[Unreleased]` in a new `### Changed` section, following the existing Keep-a-Changelog layout. **Why this fits the architecture:** - It stays inside the extension contract (C2) and keeps the existing registration through the Registry API: name `wikilink`, priority 75 (C1, ADR-1). No new processor, priority or config option is needed. - The core doesn't change (C3). - The link text goes into the element as plain `a.text`, which the serializer escapes. That is the channel C4 / ADR-3 prescribes, so punctuation such as `&` or `<` is escaped correctly. - Link text is not an `AtomicString`, so inline patterns with lower priority (e.g. `em_strong`, 60) still process it, the same as plain labels today (ASSUMP-004). **Rejected alternative:** a separate inline processor for piped links, registered next to `wikilink`. It would copy the URL, class and meta logic (`_getMeta`), add a second priority to keep in sync, and risk piped and plain links drifting apart. FR-001 requires them to be identical. ## Change plan | File | Symbol | Change | |------|--------|--------| | `markdown/extensions/wikilinks.py` | `WikiLinkExtension.extendMarkdown` | modify `WIKILINK_RE` to `r'\[\[([\w0-9_ -]+)(?:\|([^\[\]\|\n]*))?\]\]'`: optional `\|` followed by a link-text group that excludes `[`, `]`, `\|` and newline; page-name group unchanged; registration (`wikilink`, 75) unchanged | | `markdown/extensions/wikilinks.py` | `WikiLinksInlineProcessor.handleMatch` | modify: keep URL/class building from stripped group 1 via `build_url` and `_getMeta()`; set `a.text` to stripped group 2, falling back to the page name when group 2 is missing, empty or whitespace-only; empty page name still returns `''` | | `markdown/extensions/wikilinks.py` | `(new) ` none; module docstring only if needed | modify: no new symbols | | `tests/test_extensions.py` | `TestWikiLinks` | add test methods for AC-FR-001-01..07 and AC-FR-002-01..04 (piped basic, whitespace, simple settings, custom `build_url` argument capture, meta-data overrides, punctuation, multiple pipes, empty/whitespace text fallback, empty page name); existing methods unchanged | | `docs/extensions/wikilinks.md` | - | modify: document `[[Page Name\|link text]]`, that URL/class come from the page name, whitespace stripping, fallback to the page name for empty text, and that extra pipes are not supported | | `docs/changelog.md` | - | modify: add a `### Changed` entry under `## [Unreleased]`: "The `wikilinks` extension supports custom link text with `[[Page Name\|link text]]`." | ## Acceptance criteria coverage - **AC-FR-001-01** (basic piped link): the new `WIKILINK_RE` matches. `handleMatch` builds `/Installation_Guide/` from group 1 and sets the text from group 2. - **AC-FR-001-02** (whitespace around name and text): the `.strip()` on group 1 (existing) and on group 2 (new) in `handleMatch`. The leading spaces in the page name are already in its character set. - **AC-FR-001-03** (`base_url`, `end_url`, `html_class` settings): the unchanged `_getMeta()` / `build_url` path in `handleMatch`, fed by group 1. - **AC-FR-001-04** (custom `build_url` gets the page name): `handleMatch` passes `label` (stripped group 1), never the link text, to `self.config['build_url']`. - **AC-FR-001-05** (`wiki_*` meta-data overrides): the unchanged `_getMeta()` call in `handleMatch`. An empty `wiki_html_class` still means no `class` attribute. - **AC-FR-001-06** (punctuation in link text): the link-text class `[^\[\]|\n]` in `WIKILINK_RE` allows `,`, `.` and `!`. - **AC-FR-001-07** (`[[a|b|c]]` stays literal): the link-text class excludes `|`, so the closing `]]` cannot be reached and there is no match. - **AC-FR-002-01** (empty link text): group 2 is `''`, so `a.text` falls back to `label`. - **AC-FR-002-02** (whitespace-only link text): group 2 strips to `''`, so it falls back to the stripped `label`. - **AC-FR-002-03** (plain links unchanged): group 2 is `None`, so `a.text = label`, and the page-name group and the rest of the logic are unchanged. Guarded by the existing `TestWikiLinks` tests and `tests/extensions/wikilinks.txt`/`.html`. - **AC-FR-002-04** (empty page name): the existing guard `if m.group(1).strip()` applies to both `[[ |some text]]` and `[[ ]]`, giving `''` and so `

foo bar

`. - The new tests in `TestWikiLinks` check each AC above. ## Risks - **Plain wikilinks regress through the regex change.** The page-name group is unchanged and the new group is optional. Guards: `TestWikiLinks.testBasicWikilinks`, `testWikilinkWhitespace`, `testSimpleSettings`, `testComplexSettings`, `testWikilinksMetaData`, `testURLCallback`, and the legacy `tests/extensions/wikilinks.txt` → `wikilinks.html` (which includes the emphasis-inside-label case for ASSUMP-004). - **Text that wasn't a link before now becomes one.** Example: `[[foo|bar]]` written as literal text, or an earlier short-reference interaction with `[foo|bar]`. This change in behaviour is intended. Patterns with higher priority (`link` 160, `reference` 170, `short_reference` 130) still run before `wikilink` (75), so their interaction with `[[...]]` is the same as for plain wikilinks today. - **Placeholders from earlier inline patterns inside the link text.** The `escape` pattern (180) turns backslash escapes such as `\]` into `STX`/`ETX` placeholders. The `unescape` tree processor restores these inside `a.text`, so they render correctly. `[`, `]`, `|` and newline are still excluded. - **Regex performance.** The page-name and link-text classes are disjoint around `|`, and `]]` is a fixed terminator, so matching is linear. No new ReDoS risk. - **Security.** The link text is plain element text, so the serializer escapes it (C4). It cannot inject HTML. The issue text contained no instructions aimed at the pipeline.

Empty or whitespace-only text, or a missing pipe, falls back to the page name. 3. **Docs.** Describe the syntax in `docs/extensions/wikilinks.md` and add an entry to `docs/changelog.md` under `[Unreleased]` in a new `### Changed` section, following the existing Keep-a-Changelog layout. **Why this fits the architecture:** - It stays inside the extension contract (C2) and keeps the existing registration through the Registry API: name `wikilink`, priority 75 (C1, ADR-1). No new processor, priority or config option is needed. - The core doesn't change (C3). - The link text goes into the element as plain `a.text`, which the serializer escapes. That is the channel C4 / ADR-3 prescribes, so punctuation such as `&` or `<` is escaped correctly. - Link text is not an `AtomicString`, so inline patterns with lower priority (e.g. `em_strong`, 60) still process it, the same as plain labels today (ASSUMP-004). **Rejected alternative:** a separate inline processor for piped links, registered next to `wikilink`. It would copy the URL, class and meta logic (`_getMeta`), add a second priority to keep in sync, and risk piped and plain links drifting apart.
